answer.rationale: The incumbent has refused to reopen price and the contract lapses in 14 days with no auto-renew, so renew_incumbent and negotiate_terms are foreclosed this cycle; deferring risks a supply gap with zero production buffer. Switching to the low-cost vendor meets the 18% mandate, but memory_c2's positive account of a prior switch covers cost and invoicing only, not delivery reliability under a tight-capacity line — a material gap given the 94% utilization with no buffer. I verified c2 to check whether the original record contains any onboarding/delivery-risk detail the consolidated summary omitted, and c3 to see whether the second-source pattern offers a lower-risk hybrid (partial shift plus incumbent continuity) instead of a full primary switch. Given the schedule, I favor moving forward with the low-cost vendor as primary but at a standard-experiment scale rather than a full broad rollout, keeping volume commitments conservative until delivery performance is confirmed, and flagging the delivery-risk tradeoff explicitly rather than treating the cost win as settled.
